# #189 correctness review: BLOCK

Head: `703cde7710d62080907527de0e426e3d2fbe5c26`

Whole-PR review against main `d7389056ab7f8e0eaf309d1db1229c760337ba5d`, including canonical plan 224, backpressure, migration 0046 and the plan-222 seam. No product or canonical plan state was edited.

## Finding

**F001, medium: a newer own event or Working state does not veto the stale nudge.** `crates/daemon/src/idle_nudge.rs:64-74,133-142` reads Idle state from the round's registry snapshot and reads the own-event anchor before other awaited work. `:114` later calls `mark_idle_nudged`, whose insert (`crates/store/src/idle_nudges.rs:105-126`) checks only primary-key uniqueness, not whether that anchor is still the newest own event or the seat is still Idle.

A seat that starts work after the reads but before the mark can therefore receive a stale normal nudge mid-turn. The primary key prevents another send for that same old anchor; it does not make this first send correct. C31 delivers the message as a steer, so the false positive interrupts current work. The author confirmed the path and absence of a race guard/test.

**Required repair:** in the mark's own statement or transaction, insert only if the newest own event still equals the supplied anchor and the seat is still Idle. A vetoed mark must send nothing. Add controlled-race regressions that change the own-event anchor or state after the initial read, with a stable Idle/unchanged-anchor positive control. This is the same persist-time veto shape as #167 F004. PM explicitly required it in message `25af5ec9e3cc35ea-0000000000000011`; the snapshot limitation was not accepted.

## Verified behavior

- The greatest spine sequence across `seat.activity`, `report.now` and `report.state` is the anchor; its timestamp supplies the age. Idle `seat.activity` is excluded using the same predicate as plan 222. `message.pushed` is deliberately not an own event, so the nudge's delivery does not re-arm itself.
- `(seat, anchor)` is a durable primary key. `INSERT OR IGNORE`, `rows_affected > 0`, and commit precede the send. Only the insert winner proceeds. Sequential rounds and a rebuilt service retain the mark; a later own report re-arms the next stretch. This same-anchor deduplication does not close F001.
- Background queued/running owners and pending compactions suppress candidates. Both delivery and control queue kinds are checked. Eligibility read failures log and spare the seat. Plan 222 runs first, and its queued wake is then visible to the generic nudge's queue brake.
- Open roles and open claims supply candidates and rendered labels. Distinct live project primes are deduplicated; with none, the live parent is told, never the holder itself. Prime FYIs are held, while the holder receives a normal `pij-bg` message.
- Migration 0046 and `SCHEMA_VERSION=46` agree. Existing memory-turn behavior changes only by exposing `shown` within the crate. The fallback to the established word/seat predicates is the packet's explicit pre-#185 contract.

## Evidence

[CI run 42476103396](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42476103396), exact head, attempt 1: **2243 Rust cases, zero failures/errors/skips**. Artifact `13615487641`, JUnit timestamp `2026-11-08T11:32:43.644+00:00`, matches the successful Rust job. The four new daemon tests, core message test and store index test all executed. Rust lint and both Node checks also passed.

Author receipts `m224.py` and `m224.out` record all eight mutants returning exit 101 with three cases passing and one failing: mark skipped, premature cutoff, missing compaction brake, missing background brake, ignored queue peek, missing Idle-state check, idle events counted as own, and ignored project prime. The receipt's source commit `a6306ce5` is byte-identical at this head for all five relevant implementation/test files.

The unmutated four-case baseline was reported by the author but not persisted there; exact-head CI independently supplies the positive baseline. The idle-filter mutant first fails the derived-age body assertion, not a double-send assertion. The case-loop receipts preserve the failed line, not the case's panic text. No reviewer-owned mutation, build, test, dependency install or live probe was run.

## Notes and proof ceiling

**N001: overlap and failure branches are source-inspected.** The sequential test's `idle_nudged` pre-check stops a second round before insertion. It never exercises the insert-loser `false` branch. There is no dedicated overlapping-round or registry-failure receipt. The store transaction/primary key proves the implementation's same-anchor exclusion by inspection, not by an executed concurrency test. The mark records at most one attempted send, not guaranteed delivery; an interruption after commit can leave no delivered nudge, and a failed send is intentionally not retried.

**N002: index use is not a fixed row-visit bound.** The store test establishes index selection. `crates/store/src/idle_nudges.rs:24-27` still applies a residual idle-state filter while walking `seat.activity` rows backward, so a long trailing run of idle events can cost more than one row visit. Candidate selection also uses `holding.contains` on a vector while traversing the existing seat snapshot (`idle_nudge.rs:64-74`).

**Cost:** no new production loop, timer, poll or launch. This runs on the existing 60-second watchdog tick. It adds one open-holder/claim union read; when there are idle candidates, one background read and another pending-compactions read; per eligible idle candidate, up to three own-kind lookups and one mark lookup; for a due unmarked holder, a queue peek, holdings/claims reads, a mark transaction and project lookups. Sending costs one holder message plus one FYI per distinct selected prime, not invariably two messages. Live before/after measurements and disposition of the row-visit/scaling caveats remain with the performance reviewer; no such proof is claimed here.

The highest-leverage additional guard test is a bounded two-contender mark/round regression proving that only the insert winner sends, with positive own-activity re-arming. Harness observation DL-012 records that gap. Canonical plan/pressure states remain unchecked; this review does not certify whole-plan or live-deployment completion.

**Handback:** repair F001, run the new race tests and veto-removal mutants, then request review at the new final head. No local reviewer-owned tests or builds were run.
